assessment.summary: The two reportable findings have independent control owners and proportionate tactical fixes; the evidence does not justify a shared architectural hardening program.

nonNegotiables: Preserve Symbols as a lightweight local, single-user MCP-to-LSP bridge.
Keep installation and troubleshooting guidance in skills, desired state in language-servers.yaml, and runtime inspection and control in MCP resources and tools.
Prefer the smallest language-agnostic change that restores the violated invariant.
Do not introduce a managed installer, hosted service, broad workflow subsystem, or generalized security policy framework.
assumptions: No measured performance or memory budget was supplied.
Compatibility should be preserved for explicitly selected configuration and ordinary bounded diagnostic workloads.
The supplied snapshot digest represents the analyzed working tree at the target revision.

evidence.title: Workspace config auto-execution
evidence.claim: Automatically discovered workspace YAML can select a language-server command that executes without an intervening trust decision.

evidence.title: Unbounded diagnostics output
evidence.claim: Valid diagnostics from an ordinary server remain unbounded across retention, transformation, sorting, and final MCP output.

evidence.title: Repository coverage ledger
evidence.claim: The complete scan has two final findings, no deferred coverage rows, and no repeated surviving control failure connecting these two boundaries.

evidence.title: Symbols repository threat model
evidence.claim: Executable workspace policy and language-server output are distinct trust boundaries in the local single-user product.

tacticalRemediations.title: Default-deny untrusted workspace executable configuration
tacticalRemediations.securityInvariant: Automatically discovered workspace configuration cannot select an executable until the exact canonical workspace, canonical config path, and config content have been explicitly trusted; reload must re-evaluate that identity.
tacticalRemediations.recommendedShape: Keep enforcement at config-source selection. The smallest safe default is to reject auto-discovered workspace config unless it was explicitly selected or approved; if persistent convenience is retained, use a narrow user-owned content-bound approval record rather than a managed trust service.
acceptanceCriteria: An unapproved workspace-local config cannot cause a process spawn through startup, file routing, auto-detection, or reload.
Explicit CLI config and trusted shared user config retain documented behavior.
Changing config bytes, canonical path, workspace identity, or symlink target invalidates approval.
Denial is visible and fail-closed rather than silently selecting surprising executable policy.
tacticalRemediations.validationPlan: Run the finding PoC against startup and reload; add manager/session tests for denial, explicit trust, content change, canonicalization, symlink retargeting, and trusted-config compatibility.

tacticalRemediations.title: Bound diagnostic retention and model-facing output
tacticalRemediations.securityInvariant: Untrusted diagnostics are bounded before retention and transformation, and final MCP text is independently bounded with an explicit count or byte omission marker for both push and pull strategies.
tacticalRemediations.recommendedShape: Add diagnostics-specific per-URI count and message limits, bounded URI retention with empty-key deletion, omission metadata, and final rendered-count and character budgets. Reuse a small bounded-text helper only where existing local output paths already need the same primitive.
acceptanceCriteria: Push diagnostics over the ingress cap retain only bounded data and record the omitted count.
Pull diagnostics and final formatting obey independent count and character budgets.
Oversized messages are truncated explicitly, empty publications delete URI state, and URI retention is deterministically bounded.
The 10,000-error ordinary TypeScript reproduction returns bounded output with an omission marker and acceptable measured latency.
tacticalRemediations.validationPlan: Add store and formatter boundary tests for count, bytes, messages, URI eviction, push and pull behavior, then rerun the 10,000-error integration workload while recording elapsed time, output characters, retained entries, and peak memory if practical.

openQuestions: Should workspace auto-discovery be disabled until an explicit --config selection, or retained behind a narrow content-bound approval record?
What per-document, per-message, retained-URI, rendered-count, and final-character budgets preserve useful diagnostics on representative repositories?
Which existing MCP error and resource surfaces should present workspace trust denial and diagnostic omission metadata without expanding the public tool surface?
